title: Venafi Cloud issuers must move to the OutagePREDICT zone syntax

detection.reason: the issuer TYPE is projected, the zone string is not — these issuers are the ones whose zone has to be rewritten, which is the whole population

quote: The only impact to Venafi Cloud users is the change in zone syntax. The zone is now `<Application Name>\<Issuing Template Alias>` (e.g. `My Application\My CIT`).
remediation: Create an Application in OutagePREDICT with an Issuing Template and set each Venafi issuer's zone to `<Application Name>\<Issuing Template Alias>` instead of the DA Zone ID (a UUID).
verifyCommand: kubectl get issuers,clusterissuers -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.venafi.cloud) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace // "cluster")/\(.metadata.name) zone=\(.spec.venafi.zone)"'  # a zone that looks like a UUID is the old DA style and stops resolving

title: --renew-before-expiration-duration is removed — the controller will not start with it

detection.reason: checked in the cert-manager workload's container args only — a flag passed through a config file is not scanned

quote: The `--renew-before-expiration-duration` flag has been removed from the cert-manager controller, having been deprecated in the previous release.
remediation: Remove the flag from the controller's args before upgrading and set `spec.renewBefore` on the Certificates that relied on it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata as $m | .spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]? | select(test("renew-before-expiration-duration")) | "\($m.namespace)/\($m.name) \(.)"'  # each row is a controller still started with the flag; NO rows = clean

title: CertificateRequest spec and annotations become immutable — patching tooling breaks

detection.reason: CertificateRequest objects are not collected, and what breaks is the automation that edits them, which is not a cluster object at all

quote: `CertificateRequests` are now immutable - the `spec` and `metadata.annotations` fields cannot be changed after creation. They were always designed to be immutable but this behavior is now *enforced* by the cert-manager webhook.
remediation: Find anything that patches CertificateRequest spec or annotations after creation (approval tooling, GitOps reconcilers, scripts) and stop it: the webhook rejects those writes from 1.3.
verifyCommand: kubectl get certificaterequests -A -o json --show-managed-fields | jq -r '.items[] | select([.metadata.managedFields[]?.manager] | map(select(test("cert-manager|cainjector") | not)) | .[0] != null) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) managers=\([.metadata.managedFields[].manager] | unique | join(","))"'  # each row was written by something other than cert-manager; those writes are rejected after 1.3
